plan.title: Lifecycle gates fall back to hardcoded master/main instead of plan.policy.deliveryBranch

narratives.Description: Lifecycle gates fall back to hardcoded master/main instead of plan.policy.deliveryBranch
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

`plan.policy.deliveryBranch` (#3041) is the typed destination for delivered work. Most lifecycle verbs resolve it: `verify:completed-tracked`, `verify:orphan-active`, the `swarm:launch` origin-active probe (#4714), `swarm:finalize-cohort`, finalize-owed, and the session-start owed inventory. Four places bypass it and assume `master` or `main`:

1. `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` `resolveDefaultBaseRef`: `DEFT_BASE_REF` / `GITHUB_BASE_REF`, then `origin/master`, `origin/main`, `master`, `main`. Used by `verify:scope-provenance` and by the completed-write guard behind `scope:complete`.
2. `packages/core/src/evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts` `resolveDefaultBaseRef`: `origin/HEAD`, then fixed candidates.
3. `packages/core/src/branch/evaluate.ts` `DEFAULT_BRANCHES = {master, main}`: `verify:branch` and the pre-commit gate protect only those names.
4. `.githooks/pre-push`: gates pushes to the default branch only.

Effect for a consumer whose delivery branch is `develop`, `trunk`, or a long-lived integration branch:

- Locally, the merge-base lands on master, so the change set becomes the whole branch's accumulated diff and the `file_scope` fence evaluates the wrong set. CI is saved only because GitHub sets `GITHUB_BASE_REF`.
- The delivery branch is unprotected by the local commit and push gates.

## Fix

- Both resolvers: after the env overrides, try `origin/<deliveryBranch>` then `<deliveryBranch>` (via `resolveDeliveryBranch`) before the master/main fallbacks.
- `verify:branch`: add the resolved delivery branch to the protected set; keep master and main.
- `.githooks/pre-push`: protect the resolved delivery branch as well.
- Tests: a typed `deliveryBranch = develop` fixture for each of the four; the unset-policy case keeps today's behaviour.

## Acceptance

- With `plan.policy.deliveryBranch = develop` and `origin/develop` fetched, and no env overrides: `verify:scope-provenance` and `verify:evaluator-surface` compute the merge-base against `origin/develop`; `verify:branch` blocks a commit on `develop`; pre-push blocks a push to `develop`.
- With no typed policy: behaviour unchanged (git default, then master/main).
- `DEFT_BASE_REF` and `GITHUB_BASE_REF` precedence unchanged.

## Why now

Consumer-relevant on its own. It is also the prerequisite for the integration branch in #5514 (methodology for #5490): Phase 0 gates there run the released engine, so this must ship in a release before that branch opens. Small; fits the daily cadence. Lands on master through the normal process.

Refs: #5514, #5490, #3041, #3388, #4714.
